themes_detail.label: Dead Animals Spike
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints surged to 9 this week versus a baseline average of 1.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 700% spike—suggesting either a disease outbreak, pest control failure, or environmental stressor affecting Park Slope/Carroll Gardens.
evidence: 9 dead animal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.75)
Statistically significant spike classified as high-severity deviation
No recent Reddit or news coverage, suggesting story is developing and not yet public
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Department and Animal Care & Control to determine if disease, poisoning, or environmental cause is behind spike
Canvass residents in affected blocks to gather anecdotal reports and assess public health concern level

themes_detail.label: Dead/Dying Trees Emergency
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints skyrocketed 2300% this week to 3 complaints versus a baseline of 0.1 per week—the highest z-score (8.69) in the entire dataset—indicating possible disease, pest infestation, or environmental crisis affecting the neighborhood's tree canopy.
evidence: 3 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 8.69, highest spike in dataset)
2300% increase from baseline represents most statistically significant anomaly in 90-day window
Aligns with community board's recurring budget request to 'Reconstruct or upgrade a building in a park' and park infrastructure concerns
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Parks to identify which blocks are affected and whether a specific pathogen (e.g., spotted lanternfly, emerald ash borer) is driving deaths
Investigate whether recent weather events (drought, extreme cold, or flooding) are stressing trees across the district

themes_detail.label: Bike Rack Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Bike rack complaints exploded to 5 this week from a baseline of 0.4 per week—a 1233% spike—suggesting either rapid installation of defective racks, a shortage of functional parking, or a specific infrastructure failure point in the neighborhood.
evidence: 5 bike rack complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (z-score: 6.65)
1233% increase indicates concentrated, acute problem rather than chronic underinvestment
No concurrent news coverage suggests story not yet picked up by other outlets
reporting_angles: Map the 5 complaints to identify if they cluster on specific streets (e.g., Prospect Park West, 7th Avenue) or park entrances
Interview cyclists about whether a recent installation was faulty or if a popular rack location is broken

themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints reached 26 two weeks ago—a 206% spike from the 8.5 weekly baseline—indicating possible enforcement gap or contractor abuse in waste disposal practices affecting the neighborhood.
evidence: 26 illegal dumping complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 8.5 weekly baseline (z-score: 7.64)
206% surge suggests localized dumping campaign or contractor diversion rather than random incidents
Dumpster complaints also up 243% 3 weeks ago, indicating related waste management pressure
reporting_angles: Identify streets with highest dumping concentration and interview residents about whether a particular contractor or demolition project is responsible
Check DOB records: 30 full demolitions filed in last 90 days—are demolition sites inadequately securing waste?

themes_detail.label: Derelict Vehicles Accumulation
themes_detail.summary: Derelict vehicle complaints jumped to 14 last week versus a baseline of 4.2 per week—a 229% spike—suggesting either enforcement pause or a wave of vehicle abandonment linked to economic conditions or street-level disorder.
evidence: 14 derelict vehicle complaints LAST WEEK vs. 4.2 weekly baseline (z-score: 6.24)
229% increase coincides with uptick in illegal dumping and 'outside building' violations, suggesting broader street disorder
Illegal parking remains the top 311 complaint in district at 3490 total—derelict vehicles may be subset of parking enforcement collapse
reporting_angles: Request NYPD and DSNY data on vehicle tow rates to determine if enforcement has slowed
Interview residents on blocks with highest derelict vehicle concentration about whether abandoned cars are attracting other crime or disorder
